source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 180: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: compare two otherwise identical serving configurations, fixing model/tokenizer, precision, batching, hardware, software versions, and concurrency controls. Replay a fixed, stratified trace matching the short-prompt/long-generation mix, with identical lengths, arrival process, and seeds where applicable; randomize configuration order and use matched trace segments. Discard prespecified warm-up and run at least five independent paired repetitions, reporting medians, p95s, and 95% confidence intervals.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 180: at the prespecified load, the candidate increases SLO-compliant goodput by at least 10% without increasing error rate or end-to-end P99 latency by more than 5%; reject the hypothesis when the interval crosses either practical threshold. Record ingress, admission, queue release, prefill start/end, first token, every decode token, and completion timestamps. Define TTFT as first-token minus ingress, with queue-inclusive and compute-only variants; TPOT as decode time divided by generated-token count, stating first-token treatment; throughput as completed output tokens per wall-clock second; queueing as admission/release wait; and P99 end-to-end latency over all requests, with timeout/cancellation denominators explicit. Stratify by prompt length, generation length, and concurrency.

Collect correctness, errors, timeouts, cancellations, dropped requests, token counts, batch size, queue depth, GPU utilization and memory/KV-cache high-water mark, CPU/RAM, power, temperature, and throttling from synchronized request-level traces. Confounders include cache/order effects, background load, autoscaling, thermal throttling, compilation/GC, network variance, retries, and model or software drift; randomize, block, or report them. Stop or roll back on correctness regression, OOM/instability, thermal or power risk, or repeated SLO violation, using a canary first. Evidence required: versioned trace and manifests, raw lifecycle traces and telemetry, correctness labels, and paired repetition-level data. Platform-specific conclusions remain unverified until those artifacts are reviewed.
risks: Synthetic prompt omits hardware, stack, SLO, and correctness-oracle details.
The 10%/5% thresholds are proposed assumptions, not measured facts.
Replay and telemetry synchronization may bias results.
evidence_required: Versioned stratified workload trace and configuration manifests
Per-request timestamps, outcomes, raw resource telemetry, and exclusion log
At least five independent paired repetitions with interval method documented
